hl: A vat still holding water, a century on
sub: Florida DEP photograph. The stepped cattle exit at the far end matches the 1911 federal specification.
Concrete steps out of the dip. A state inspector stands at the head of the vat.
Florida's own report records disused vats reused as pesticide-mixing areas and as swimming holes for children.

hl: Twelve feet of concrete in the grass
sub: Hidden by growth. The same floor length as the concrete base found above Ladera Ranch.
Sites like this are why 11 of 12 tested Florida vats failed the soil standard for arsenic.
Timber rails guided the herd in. At Ladera Ranch, iron pipe rails still lead up to the concrete.
Florida found its vats, fenced them off, and cleaned them up. California never inventoried a single one.
